_readme: First Mate weight-change log. Documented in skills/first-mate/SKILL.md's 'Weight tuning approach' section. Every change to a signal weight or proximity threshold in effectiveHeat() should get appended here so we can retrospectively evaluate whether a change actually helped or hurt over 30+ days of archive. Append-only. Never edit history. Every entry: date_changed (ISO), signal, change_type (weight | proximity | vocab | activation), old_value, new_value, rationale, expected_hit_rate_delta, first_mate_notes, archive_baseline (which archive dates were the 'before' state).

changes.rationale: compute_persistence_flags in model_signals.py required exactly 3 consecutive prior days of archive to declare persistence. Randy's archive has multi-day gaps (missing nightlies from proxy/retry issues), so the 'missing a day → return []' early-exit fired every day and the signal was permanently 0. Rewrote to tolerate gaps: take the most recent N snapshots within a 2N-day lookback window. Same semantic intent ('an SST break that stayed put over multiple days') but measured against snapshots we actually have.
changes.expected_hit_rate_delta: unknown — signal was structurally dormant so we have zero historical data. First 30 days after this ship give us the baseline. Expect it fires on 0-5% of zones per day when persistent breaks form near canyons/ledges.
changes.first_mate_notes: This isn't a weight tune — it's a bug fix that turned a dormant signal into an active one. Do NOT count the first 30 days of firings as 'the signal is helpful' vs any real baseline; instead, use those days to establish what a 'normal' firing rate looks like. Only after we have 30+ days should we start asking whether persistence-boosted zones outperform.
changes.archive_baseline: 2026-07-25 through 2026-09-09 — 28 snapshots, all with persistenceBoost=0 for every zone

changes.rationale: Aligned proximity radius with the sistem signals (sstGradientBoost and sshaBoost both use 15 nm as the standard 'oceanographic feature close enough to matter' cutoff, per the First Mate signal-backlog documentation). 12 nm on persistenceBoost was inherited without rationale.
changes.expected_hit_rate_delta: roughly 1.5x more zones per persistent break can qualify (15 nm radius circle area = 1.56x the 12 nm area). Not a weight-value change — same +0.3 boost, wider trigger radius.
changes.first_mate_notes: This ships together with the activation fix above, so we can't disentangle their individual effects — but that's fine because the goal is 'signal now fires when it should'. Both changes applied to client (fish-finder.src.html persistenceBoost) and server (archive.py _persistence_boost) for parity.
changes.archive_baseline: same as above — no data at either radius before this ship
